change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with a SafeParse result object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29`), so `key` here is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Line 100 writes that object to `credential.key`. The next time the service is built, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws, because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are now nested under `data`. This runs on every Google token refresh, whether or not credential sharing is enabled, so every Google Calendar user breaks after their first refresh. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or keep `googleCredentialSchema.parse`).

findings.title: Computed schema keys evaluate to the literal "[object Object]"
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both become the property name `"[object Object]"`. The second one overwrites the first, so the schema is really `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Zod's `z.object` strips unknown keys, so in sync mode every expiry field (`expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, ...) is dropped from `data`. For example, Office 365 merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:264), so the stored expiry never moves forward and the token counts as expired on every call. Use `.passthrough()` (or `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).catchall(z.unknown())`) instead of computed keys.

findings.title: Sync path returns a fetch Response, but several callers expect SDK or axios shapes
findings.body:
In sync mode this returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, and the callers were written for other return shapes:
- Google (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94`) reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a Response, so line 95 throws.
- HubSpot (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192-198`) treats it as a `HubspotToken` and writes the Response object into `credential.key`.
- Zoho Bigin (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`) and Zoho CRM read `.data.error` as if it were an axios response.

Only the fetch-based adapters (Office 365, Zoom, Webex, Lark) work with the sync endpoint. Either return parsed JSON in a shape every caller agrees on, or adapt each caller.

findings.title: Credential id passed where the user id is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends its third argument to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). Here it gets `credentialId` (`credential.id`, line 53), so the parent application gets asked for tokens for the wrong user, which can mean another user's tokens. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`. Pass `credential.userId` here too (it has to be threaded into `refreshAccessToken`).

findings.title: `prisma` is used without an import
findings.body: This file never imports `prisma` (imports at lines 1-20), so this line resolves to the global `prisma`. `packages/prisma/index.ts:56-59` sets `globalThis.prisma` only conditionally (the dev-only hot-reload cache). In production, every Salesforce client construction would then throw a ReferenceError after the token fetch. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every construction, ignores the sync endpoint, and keeps using the stale token
findings.body:
Three problems with this block:
- `getClient` now calls Salesforce's token endpoint on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction, with no expiry check.
- It doesn't go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the sync endpoint is never used for Salesforce, yet in sync mode `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to the minimal schema and drops `instance_url`. The saved key then has no `instance_url`, and the next construction builds a connection with `instanceUrl: undefined`.
- The new access token is saved to the database, but the `jsforce.Connection` at lines 101-108 is still built from the old `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`.

Also, `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile: HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText. Use `response.ok`.

findings.title: Malformed body or bad ciphertext surfaces as an unhandled 500
findings.body: `parse` (line 31), `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` (lines 57-59) all throw on bad input, and nothing catches them, so the caller gets a generic 500 with no message. The handler also accepts any HTTP method. Consider `safeParse`, returning 400 on decrypt/parse failure, and restricting to POST.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==`
findings.body: This endpoint can overwrite any user's credentials. The shared secret is checked with plain string inequality, which isn't constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and reject the request when the header is missing or is an array.

contracts.action: Google token refresh now goes through refreshOAuthTokens + parseRefreshTokenResponse before saving
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code: googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) stored the parsed data
contracts.before_after: Before: the key was the parsed credential object. After: the key is the SafeParse wrapper {success,data}.
contracts.visible_effect: After the first refresh, line 75 parse throws on the next load, and Google Calendar busy times/events fail for the user
contracts.failure_mode: In sync mode res is a fetch Response with no .data, so line 95 throws a TypeError. It's caught at line 103 and the auth is returned with the stale token, silently.

contracts.action: Sync-endpoint refresh for HubSpot and Zoho Bigin
contracts.before_after: In sync mode the caller receives a fetch Response instead of a HubspotToken or axios response
contracts.visible_effect: HubSpot stores the Response object as the credential key. Bigin reads .data.error on undefined and throws.
contracts.failure_mode: HubSpot's error is swallowed by the catch at lines 203-205 (log only)

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient performs a token refresh and DB update on every construction
contracts.equivalent_path: Other adapters refresh only when the token has expired
contracts.before_after: Saves the new token to the DB but builds the connection from the old credentialKey
contracts.visible_effect: Extra token call per booking; the jsforce connection uses the stale access token
contracts.failure_mode: A non-OK status throws HttpError, which rejects this.conn, so every Salesforce operation fails

contracts.action: New webhook endpoint creates/updates credentials from an encrypted payload
contracts.before_after: Validates the secret, the user and the app, decrypts the keys, then finds the credential by userId+appId and updates it or creates one
contracts.visible_effect: The user's installed app gets the shared credentials
contracts.failure_mode: zod, decrypt and JSON errors throw an unhandled 500

summary: Blocker: Google token refresh now saves the whole SafeParse result object (`{success, data}`) as the credential key. This happens even with credential sharing off, so every Google Calendar user breaks after their first token refresh. The sync-mode helpers also have problems. The minimal schema's computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]", so expiry fields get stripped. `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response that the Google, HubSpot and Zoho callers can't consume. Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the user id. Salesforce uses `prisma` without importing it, refreshes on every construction, and builds its connection with the stale token.
